- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent low, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at +10% above prior peak to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overestimate; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias for 3–7 day horizon.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days falling after peak), reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 5+ consecutive days > +1% daily), reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence in trend continuation.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.11 to -0.61), adjust forecast to reflect 2–3 day lag in sentiment impact, reducing forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
